english.title: Manufacturer/importer/supplier fail to test and examine substance to ensure it was safe when handled at work premises

additionalkeywords.additionalkeyword: Health and Safety at Work Act 1974

english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being the

(A)_[manufacturer]_
(B)_[importer]_
(C)_[supplier]_

of a substance, namely **(..SPECIFY SUBSTANCE..), failed to discharge your duty to carry out or arrange for the carrying out of such testing and examination as was necessary to ensure, so far as was reasonably practicable, that the substance would be safe and without risks to health at all times when it was being used, handled, processed, stored or transported by a person at work or at premises to which section 4 of the Health and Safety at Work etc Act 1974 applied
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 6(4)(b) and 33(1)(a) of, and Schedule 3A to, the Health and Safety at Work etc Act 1974.

english.notes:
(i) See section 2(2) of the Act for examples of the extent of the employer's duty.
(ii) Proceedings for an offence shall not, in England and Wales, be instituted except by an inspector of the Environment Agency or the Natural Resources Body for Wales or by or with the consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions, see section 38 of the Health and Safety at Work etc Act 1974.

other.penalty:
Either way -
Summary: 6/12 months imprisonment and / or a fine.
Indictment: 2 years imprisonment and / or a fine.

The maximum penalty on summary conviction is 6 months for offences committed before 2nd May 2002; for offences committed on or after that date it may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see Schedule 3A to the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974 and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2020.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
